To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microporous activated carbons with uniform micropore distribution are promising candidates for high power hybrid capacitors with binary transition metal oxide.
the hybrid configuration of micro porous activated carbon with nanostructured MnCo 2 oxide has been demonstrated as a high powered hybrid supercapcapitor.
the hybrid capacitor of mAC||KCl||MnCo2O4 shows superior rate capability in comparison with other hybrid capacitors of mAC||TEABF4||MnCo_2O_4 and mAC||2SO4||MnCO_2O_2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a high power and high energy hybrid supercapacitors by coupling a high surface area, uniformly sized microporous activated carbons with nanostructured binary metal oxide MnCo 2.O 4.
the design of a high performance hybrid supercapacitive electrode by combining the advantages of microporous carbon and nanostructured binary metal oxide.
a new approach of hybridizing microporous carbon with pseudocapacitance material to achieve a high power rate capability and high energy density.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microporous activated carbons with high specific surface area and high microporosity are the most promising electrode material for the development of high power supercapacitors.
the hybrid configuration of mAC with MnCo 2 Oxide is a viable approach to design high power and high energy density capacitors.

a hybrid supercapacitors of mAC||KCl||MnCo2O4 exhibits the best capacitive performance with the specific capacitance, 160.8 F g −1, specific energy, 4.8 Wh kg -1 and specific power, 11.2 kW kg − 1 at the high current rate of 10 A g -1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hybrid configuration of micro porous activated carbon with nanostructured pseudcapacitive metal oxide can be used to develop high power hybrid capacitor.

the micropores are not the only key factor to enhance the capacitive properties of carbon based electrodes, rather it should be combined with the nanostructure of pseudocapacative material for the high power and energy density applications.
the microporous activated carbons with uniformly sized micropores are the promising electrode material for high power hybrid supercapacitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hybrid configuration of microporous carbon and nanostructured pseudocapiative metal oxide can significantly enhance the power rate capability of supercapacitor without sacrificing its energy density.

the hybrid supercapacitors with micro porous activated carbon electrodes and nanostructured binary metal oxide pseudocapacitor electrodes are capable of delivering high energy and high power simultaneously.
the high rate capability of the hybrid capacitors can be achieved by using the microporous activated carbons as the electrodes.
